title: Paper Path · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Paper Path · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Place two sheets and a small paper ball on a clear table. The lead folds the sheets into a continuous channel and rolls the paper ball through it. The ball travels from one end to the other while staying in the channel. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Three sheets of paper.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Paper Path, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The ball travels from one end to the other while staying in the channel.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: The ball travels from one end to the other while staying in the channel.
